summary.intent: Execute a handoff to fix four CipherBox issues (#2016, #2021, #1956, #2017) via three parallel background lanes, drive each PR through review, gates, CI, and merge, then write the follow-on ADR documentation for the durable design changes those PRs introduced.
summary.outcome: All three PRs (2059, 2060, 2063) merged closing all four issues with main green (2800 tests, clippy clean); two ADR docs PRs (2081 ADR 0054, 2082 ADR 0055) were written, fixed for quality-gate compliance, rebased through an ADR-index collision, merged (2081) and had their status flipped to Accepted, with 2082's flip still landing at session end.

repo: cipherbox-engine crypto/loss-path bugs cluster around the retire ledger and sequence floor: an acknowledged-but-unconfirmed PUT that ties at its own sequence needs a durable 'acknowledged sequence' mark per node (cbx/ra/<owner>/<node>) or a later record can resurrect a retired/dropped version's content.

The retire ledger entry format was extended to a versioned (0x02) grammar carrying an origin byte, node id, owed/manifest byte counts, and a target CID+pinnedBytes list, while still decoding legacy 68-byte prune-debt entries for backward compatibility.

engine/src/sync/tick.rs's run_past_deadline and refresh.rs's ForcedPass::landed each hand-rolled a poll_fn race that duplicates the existing record_plane::within combinator (or futures_util::select), and this duplication recurred across at least 3 call sites before being folded.

Staleness rung (Reconciling/Fresh/Stale) was previously computed on read (status()/snapshot()), which meant a read during a pass could get stuck displaying 'reconciling' forever if no later event replaced it; fix bounds Reconciling to one refresh_deadline (30s) from pass start via SyncStatus::observe/reported.

Cut-epoch floor checks before signing existed in only one place (RootPublish::check_publishable); the fix work found it needed replicating to net/rotation.rs and sync/drain.rs, and CodeRabbit/altitude review flagged the three copies for future drift risk.

ADR 0053 (merged as PR 2066) re-pads the ADR index markdown table, causing later ADR PRs that also add an index row to conflict; each new ADR PR should rebase and re-insert its row rather than assume no reflow.

code.finding: run_past_deadline starts a new 30s timer on every pass (poll/focus/wake); on web the setTimeout-based scheduler seam never clears the timer on drop, leaking a Promise+2 wasm-bindgen closures per pass until the 30s expires.

staleness_now took borrow_mut on every read just to write `reported`, causing reads to have side effects; refactored via SyncStatus::observe/Cell to keep reads pure and dedupe StalenessChanged events by last-reported rung, not last-event rung.
FolderState carried both `is_scope_root: bool` and `carried_cut_epoch: Option<u64>` with an unenforced invariant between them; consolidated into FolderState::commitment as the single source of truth.
tombstone_of: BTreeMap<[u8;16], bool> duplicated the existing tombstoned: BTreeSet<[u8;16]> (the set is just the true-valued keys of the map).

workflow: Multi-lane background agent orchestration: launch N independent fix lanes with worktree isolation + draft PRs, then serialize the shared CodeRabbit review slot across lanes rather than requesting concurrently.

Nested review agents (simplify: reuse/simplification/efficiency/altitude, security, crypto-privacy, code-review) spawned by a lane all route their task-notifications to the orchestrator, which must hold partial results until all N arrive before forwarding a consolidated decision back to the lane.
Background Bash tool calls have a 10-minute cap; a script needing to wait past that (e.g. for a CodeRabbit slot ~11 min away) must be relaunched as a detached process instead.

When an agent hits the Opus session rate limit mid-task, it dies leaving a clean worktree with a local uncommitted-safe commit; resuming after reset requires explicitly telling it to rebase onto the new main before its single push.

GitHub PR body reads over GraphQL can silently return an empty string under rate limiting; a follow-on patch based on that empty read wipes the real PR body — always verify a non-empty read (or use REST) before patching PR bodies, and abort on empty reads.
Squash-merging PRs and then fast-forwarding local main plus removing lane worktrees/branches is the standard lane-closure sequence, followed by a monitored post-merge clippy+full-test run on main.
